subject: Unexpected mid-cycle overage — Helix Health embeddings (possible double-counting)
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixhealth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@helixhealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Unplanned mid-cycle charge — need explanation

Ben —

We just woke up to a mid-cycle charge for $12,450 related to embeddings usage. That’s roughly 4x our historical week-over-week usage and we didn’t deploy anything that would justify it. I attached a CSV snapshot of hourly usage (usage_snapshot_20270502.csv) — you can see a very sharp spike starting 2027-05-01 02:00 UTC.

Two immediate asks: can you confirm what metric we were billed against (tokens vs embeddings vector units), and whether you can put a temporary hold on further collection while we get to the bottom of this? This is a production account and a surprise charge like this will require an internal escalation on our side.

Thanks — we’re stuck on a compliance review, so a quick triage would help.

Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
Helix Health

Attachments: usage_snapshot_20270502.csv (CSV, 32KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixhealth.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unplanned mid-cycle charge — need explanation

On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 9:22 AM Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixhealth.ai> wrote:
> Ben —
> 
> We just woke up to a mid-cycle charge for $12,450 related to embeddings usage...

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in Soojin from SE and Marissa from Finance so we can do a fast triage and isolate billing vs ingestion causes.

Immediate steps from our side:
- I’ve asked Finance to place a provisional hold on collections for this invoice while we investigate (Marissa, can you confirm?).
- Soojin will run a usage-level audit (request IDs, session ids, regions) to see whether requests were duplicated across regions or retried.
- If it’s customer-side (e.g., backfill job or multi-region replay) we’ll document evidence and provide an adjusted usage export for your audit.

Can you confirm whether you were running any backfill jobs, multi-region ingest, or SDK upgrades around 2027-05-01 00:00–06:00 UTC? Also, if you can forward any example request IDs from your logs (even a few), that would speed up root cause analysis.

I’ll keep you posted today — propose a 30-minute call at 1:30pm PT if that works.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment references: usage_snapshot_20270502.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unplanned mid-cycle charge — need explanation

Ben / Jordan —

I pulled a detailed call-level export for Helix Health for the apparent spike window (2027-05-01 00:00–08:00 UTC). Preliminary findings: there are clusters of identical payloads with different request_ids but the same session_id and near-identical timestamps (within 250ms). That pattern is consistent with an SDK retry path that fails to include an idempotency token.

Notes from the export:
- Billed metric: embeddings vector units (per-indexed-document vectors).
- Spike is concentrated in us-west-2 and us-east-1, often overlapping.
- Example evidence piece (trimmed): request_id: 03e8a1f2, session_id: sess-9a7f, ts: 2027-05-01T02:12:15.122Z; duplicate request_id set also seen: 03e8a1f3, 03e8a1f4 with same payload. (See duplicate_ids_sample.txt attached.)

This looks like a multi-region failover combined with an SDK client that retries on transient socket errors but doesn’t attach the idempotency key, causing the service to treat retries as new ingest events. We shipped an SDK patch (1.2.5) that requires passing X-Idempotency-Key for batch ingestion; older 1.2.4 would retry without it. Do you know which SDK version your ingestion clients were using?

Short-term mitigations we can do immediately:
- We can exclude calls that match the duplicate-signature heuristic from the billing export for a provisional adjustment (we’ll need explicit sign-off from Finance).
- We can provide a filtered usage export that collapses duplicates by session_id+payload-hash.

Jordan — if you can share 1–2 full request IDs and confirm SDK version we’ll finalize the filtered export. I’ve attached a small sample showing the duplicate clusters.

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: duplicate_ids_sample.txt (text, 8KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unplanned mid-cycle charge — need explanation

Team —

Thanks for the quick analysis, Soojin. Finance is comfortable proposing a provisional credit while the technical audit completes. My suggested approach:

1) Provisional credit: apply a 75% provisional credit on the overage line ($12,450 * 0.75 = $9,337.50) immediately to prevent collections and to give Helix runway. We’ll mark it "provisional, subject to final audit" on the invoice.
2) Full audit: compile the filtered usage export (collapse duplicates) and recon the billed units vs the collapsed units — if the audit shows the duplication accounts for less than the provisional credit, we’ll issue a reconciled invoice/credit. If it’s more, we’ll increase the credit retroactively.
3) Docs & remediation: include the SDK idempotency guidance (link above) and recommend upgrading to 1.2.5+ and enabling client-side idempotency keys.

Jordan — can you confirm acceptance of the provisional credit flow so we can issue a formal invoice adjustment and note it in your billing portal? Once you confirm I’ll prepare a credit memo and provisional invoice adjustment (attachment: provisional_credit_calc.xlsx).

Rishi, FYI in case we need to escalate the SLA credit or sign an MSA amendment.

Marissa Cole
Senior Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: provisional_credit_calc.xlsx (Excel, 14KB)
